summary: Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak in 1928, later serving as lecturer (1946) and professor (1956–1975) at the same institution.

Anthony Hendrik Nicolaas Verwey worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University, and held a post at the National Museum of Ethnology from 1947 to 1981.

Anthony J. Alston specialized in Indology and philosophy. He was a pupil of Hari Prasad Shastri around 1948–1956 and completed his PhD under T. R. V. Murti at Banaras Hindu University around 1959–1964.

Anthony Kennedy Warder was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at SOAS under William Stede and John Brough (~1949–1954). He held posts at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963) and the University of Toronto (1963–1990).

Anthony Tribe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Bristol and Oxford (DPhil, 1995) under Alexis Sanderson. He taught at the University of Montana (attested 1997) and joined the University of Arizona (attested 2020).
Anthony W. Barber is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1984 and held a post at the University of Calgary (attested 1998).
Antoine Bazin was a French sinologist who studied under Stanislas Julien at the Collège de France around 1832. He later served as secrétaire-adjoint of the Société Asiatique in 1852.

Antoine Cabaton worked in linguistics, history, and Indology, studying at the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi and the École du Louvre. His career included posts at the BNF (1897), EFEO (~1900–1902), INALCO (1907), and École Nationale de la France d'Outre-Mer (~1914–1933).

Antoine Grégoire specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies, completing degrees at Liège, Leipzig, Munich, and Paris. He held professorships at the University of Liège (1905–1942) and the Université libre de Bruxelles (1936–1945).
Antoine Lutz studied under doctoral supervisor Francisco Varela at Pierre and Marie Curie University, where he earned his PhD.

Antoine Marie Tabard was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He taught sciences at St. Joseph's University (1891–1924) and founded The Mythic Society in 1909, serving as its president in 1910.

Antoine Meillet was a linguist also active in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Abel Bergaigne (~1887–1888) and Ferdinand de Saussure (~1889–1891), later training many prominent linguists.

Antoine Mosac was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He served as Superior of the Jesuit Mission of Chandernagore in 1742 and Superior of the Paris Foreign Missions Society from 1775 to 1777.
Antoine-Gaspard Bellin, who worked in Indology, earned a Dr.iuris from the University of Lyon by 1839. He served as a civil judge and librarian at the Tribunal civil de Lyon.

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held chairs in Arabic (from 1795) and Persian (from 1806) at INALCO, and served as president of the Société Asiatique (1822–1829, 1832–1834).

Antoine-Jean Saint-Martin was a linguist and historian who studied at INALCO under Silvestre de Sacy. He co-founded the Société Asiatique (1820) and held posts at the foreign ministry (~1814–1820), Imprimerie Nationale (~1820–1832), and Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal (1824).
Antoine-Louis Henri de Polier was an Indologist who served as a Colonel in the East India Company and studied under the traditional teacher Ramchandra.

Antoine-Léonard Chézy was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Silvestre de Sacy and Louis-Mathieu Langlès. He was the Sanskrit chair at the Collège de France (1815–1832) and professor of Persian at INALCO (1824–1827).

Anton Boller was an Austrian linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna in 1831. He spent his career at the University of Vienna, serving as Dozent and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics from 1845 onward.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin (1828–1831). He later lectured there (1849–1852) and held a post at the Royal Danish Library.
